title: The ViSta Method for Stacking in the Fourier Domain and its Application to the Dusty Star-forming Galaxies in the ALMA Science Archive
question: Can visibilities of galaxies at different redshifts be stacked directly in the Fourier domain after shifting them to the rest frame (ViSta), and does this recover faint line emission better than image-plane stacking, as tested on simulated data and on CO(3-2) in a sample of dusty star-forming galaxies from the ALMA archive?

data.arrays: 12-m antennas assumed for the primary-beam model; ALMA 12-meter array
data.angular_resolution: 0.25 to 2.8 arcsec across the real sample; worst resolution (common convolution beam) 5.063 x 2.820 arcsec

what.value: Spectroscopic redshifts of the sources (from ALMA spectral scans), plus SED constraints and line detections for the sample

evidence.quote: which provided spectroscopic redshifts through ALMA spectral scans

external_data.citation: BEARS I, II and III (cite: bearsI; bearsII; bearsIII)

what.value: Literature line properties used as a consistency comparison for the stacked CO(3-2) line

evidence.quote: The resulting line properties are broadly consistent with other estimates in the literature

recipe.goal: Select sample and obtain calibrated measurement sets
recipe.method: 21 DSFGs with CO(3-2) from ALMA archival projects; calibrated MSs retrieved (mostly) from the EU ARC CalMS service; coordinates and observations checked
key_parameters: Unlensed or moderately resolved sources only; spectroscopic redshift required

recipe.goal: Center each source at the phase center and correct for primary beam
recipe.method: phaseshift to the source position, then PHASE_DIR/REFERENCE_DIR/DELAY_DIR and POINTING directions set to zero; visibilities divided by the Gaussian primary-beam response at the source offset
key_parameters: Primary beam PB(theta) = exp[-4 ln2 (theta nu d / 1.2 c)^2] for a 12-m antenna
assumptions: Primary beam approximated by a normalized symmetric Gaussian

recipe.goal: Shift visibilities to the rest frame
recipe.method: Frequencies and dependent SPECTRAL_WINDOW parameters scaled by (1+z); UVW, antenna positions and dish diameter divided by (1+z)
assumptions: Spectroscopic redshift of each source is accurate

recipe.goal: Rebin and regrid the spectral axis to a common grid
recipe.method: mstransform to a common spectral resolution (optional Hanning smoothing first); flagged dummy channels added with flagdata and concat so all MSs have equal channel count, then mstransform to cut and regrid
key_parameters: Common finer spectral grid set by the dataset with the highest native resolution

recipe.goal: Rescale flux to a common reference redshift and concatenate
recipe.method: Each visibility multiplied by w = D_L^2(z_source)/D_L^2(z_common) x (1+z_common)/(1+z_source), then concat; OBSERVATION table unified so all scans form one observation
key_parameters: Reference redshift z_common = 2.5 for the real sample
assumptions: No lensing-magnification or other flux-normalization correction applied to the real sample
Flat LambdaCDM with h approx 0.67, Omega_m approx 0.3, Omega_Lambda approx 0.7

recipe.method: Per-channel weight w(nu) = sqrt(N_coverage(nu)/N), with weights of repeated observations of the same source divided by the number of repeats

recipe.goal: Extract the stacked CO(3-2) spectrum and fit the line
recipe.method: Three methods: ViSta-uvFit (uvmultifit with a Gaussian model, spatial parameters free in each channel, one fit per channel); ViSta-ImFit (tclean of stacked MS, flux from moment-0-derived size); ImSta-ImFit (classical image stacking). A Gaussian (mu, sigma, A, continuum C) is fitted to each stacked spectrum; a continuum image was also made as post-processing
key_parameters: uvmultifit with OneFitPerChannel = True, write = residuals; Gaussian or delta model
Natural weighting, Hogbom, cell = 1/5 of the beam major axis
assumptions: Source size from zero-order moment maps for the image-plane methods

recipe.goal: Compare visibility and image stacking SNR at the worst common resolution
recipe.method: Convolve all datasets to the worst angular resolution, then compare spectra and RMS noise of ViSta-ImFit and ImSta-ImFit
One fourth of the available data of each observation selected, analysis repeated at native resolution and at the worst resolution

recipe.goal: Validate ViSta on simulated ALMA datasets
recipe.method: 50 mock sources per case simulated with simobserve plus custom noise; compare ViSta-uvFit, ViSta-ImFit and ImSta-ImFit for unresolved and resolved (5 arcsec FWHM) sources at native size, fitted size and lowest resolution, and for continuum
key_parameters: Unresolved case: flux taken as peak value in the image; resolved case: flux in circular aperture of radius 3 sigma of the Gaussian
assumptions: Continuum subtraction and weighting skipped; no redshift flux-scaling correction because all mock fluxes equal
